label: sparse conjunction: g/i/j/x/d/p input early in original phase after k/r, in b/g/q/l/w-initial sequences (weak)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps) that fires weakly (mean 0.13, max 0.25). About 75% of its mass is in the original phase at positions 3-6. It favors input tokens g (11.7x lift), i, j, x, d and p, especially when the previous one or two inputs are k or r, often repeated (k k, r r), and when the sequence starts with b, g or q. About 25% of the mass is in the copy phase, mostly with g as input near recall_idx 2. It almost never fires at t=0-1, at the delimiter, or on digits, and it is rarer in sequences with many digits. No predicate came close to isolating it: the input-token set alone has 84% recall but 0.2% precision, and adding first-token and k/r-history conditions only reaches F1 of about 0.15. This looks like a distributed hidden-state direction, not a clean token or position detector. No magnitude claims were checked.
